name: element.get
title: Get element
summary: One element with text, properties, relations, version (and on request its date), hints, which variants replace or exclude it, and the references of its acceptance criteria for test names.

view.description: The view to show the element in. Not taken yet: it gives `input.invalid`.

versionDate.description: Also give the date of the version (`versionDate`, D-013, ADR-0005), read from the Git history. Without it no git runs and `versionDate` is left out, so opening an element stays fast (SR-082 AK3); the app asks for the date in a second call.

hintDates.description: Date only the outdated relations and inline references and the changed core requirements of replacements among the hints (`relation.outdated`, `variant.core-changed`: `storedDate`, `currentDate`, `storedCommit`, `currentCommit` and both dates with their commits in the message, D-013, ADR-0005, #252), not the version of the element itself. Git reads only the histories of their targets, and none when the element has no outdated relation; the app asks for it in a second call after the element is shown, only for an element with such hints (SR-110 AK2, SR-082 AK3). `versionDate` dates these hints too.

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (for example one copy of a file whose UUID another file shares, SR-088; ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#255). Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

file.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its file, relative to its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#255). Give repository too when the same path is in several repositories; when several elements are still left, the error is ref.ambiguous with them.

element.description: Text, properties, version (in normal form n2, the form the tool writes; a stored version of n1 is compared in its own form, ADR-0005) and, with the input `versionDate`, its date (`versionDate`, D-013, ADR-0005: the committer date in UTC of the newest commit that started this version; null for content no commit has and when Git cannot tell, including a git call that timed out; left out without the input), the own relations, the successors of a superseded element (SR-072 AK3), the hints of the element (none while the metamodel is not valid; also `variant.superseded-in-validity`, SR-040 AK3, `variant.target-not-core` for a replacement or exclusion of the element that names no core requirement, SR-041 AK8, the outdated relations and inline references of the element, `relation.outdated`, and the changed core requirements of its replacements, `variant.core-changed` (SR-045), at a variant the core requirements changed or new since its newest baseline, `variant.core-changed-since-baseline` and `variant.core-new-since-baseline` (SR-103), SR-026 AK3, whose messages name the dates of both versions only with the input `versionDate` or `hintDates`, and `metamodel.meaning-unassigned` when no property has the meaning title) and `readOnly`, always given (unknown type, invalid metamodel or a repository folder that cannot be written). An element with a value that counts and has no normal form (`.inf`, `.nan`, ADR-0005) comes without `version` and `versionDate`, with a `file.faulty` warning last in its hints that says why (ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#276). The incoming relations of every kind: `trace.neighbourhood` with `direction: down`. `verification`, for an element whose type has the meaning `requirement`: its verification status in each view it is in by the view rule (SR-043, SR-047 AK3), as evidence.status gives it (SR-031), with the indirect verification and the children that are missing (SR-034). `validation`: its validation status (SR-038), for every need and for a requirement with a validation record (a validation record of any other element counts for no status, SR-038 AK5), separate from `verification`. `replacedBy` and `excludedBy`, for a core requirement: the variants that replace it (with the replacing requirement) and those that exclude it (SR-046 AK3).

fileSha256.description: Of the file this answer was read from, for expectedFileSha256 of element.update (SR-106).

criterionReferences.description: The acceptance criteria of the element as its file holds them now, each with number, criterion key, text and the reference for a test name (SR-205 AK1); left out for an element that is no requirement or has none.

names.description: The elements the element names by UUID only, each once in the order first named: the variants of `validity`, `replacedBy` and `excludedBy`, the replacements and the views of `verification` (SR-046 AK1/AK2, SR-047 AK3, ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#588). Left out when it names none.

incomplete.description: A repository of the workspace is not here (SR-006 AK2): replacements, exclusions and records stored there are missing.
